newsitem.title: THAILAND: Anand says Thailand facing its greatest crisis.
newsitem.headline: Anand says Thailand facing its greatest crisis.

text.p: Former Thai prime minister Anand Panyarachun said the need to seek assistance from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) shows Thailand is facing its greatest crisis, the Bangkok Post reported on Tuesday.

Anand, one of the country's most respected statesmen who was twice prime minister, said the move demonstrated that Thailand was confronted by a serious, deep-rooted crisis of faith and political bankruptcy.

"There is nowhere else in this world where people have lost all faith in their own government and prefer their financial and monetary affairs to be managed by the IMF," Anand told Bangkok Post staff at a ceremony to receive the Ramon Magsaysay Award for government service.
Thailand is expected on Tuesday to announce a package of economic measures recommended by the IMF to try and resuscitate the economy which is growing at its slowest pace in a decade.
The package is expected to include a standby credit line and/or loans to help boost the economy. Analysts say Thailand needs $10 billion to $20 billion to get the economy back on track.

The country has nearly $90 billion in foreign currency loans, about $40 billion of which are short-term and come due by the end of the year. Analysts say there are worries that creditors may not roll over loans because they do not have confidence in the country's ability to solve its economic problems.
Anand said the fact that the government needed assistance from the IMF showed the country was bankrupt.
"This shows that we cannot solve our own problems because there is no faith in the existing system," said Anand.
He blamed the current administration of premier Chavalit Yongchaiyudh and the previous government of Banharn Silpa-archa for causing the crisis.
"We have been building up our nation for the past 40-50 years but in two and a half years, in two governments, all the effort went to waste."

"I have never seen Thailand in such a serious case," said Anand, who last served as prime minister in 1992 following a political crisis. He stayed in Thailand's top office until elections were held and Chuan Leekpai was elected.

Anand said Thailand's need to seek an IMF rescue package also eroded its international standing, noting that Singapore's deputy prime minister said at the weekend that Singaporeans should draw lessons from Thailand's economic difficulties.
